title: Separate lease execution from possession and commencement
prompt: At the stated cutoff, classify the land-control state and identify which obligations can enter a cash-flow model. The lease is signed, but no evidence says the commencement conditions have been satisfied.

observations.content: The parties executed a ground lease on the effective date. Their earlier memorandum of understanding expired when the lease was executed.

The lease commencement date is the day after four items are satisfied: prior leases end, existing encumbrances are resolved or waived, the tenant receives or waives a surface waiver, and a Phase One subtenant term sheet is executed and delivered. A commencement notice and recorded lease memorandum evidence that date.
Before commencement, the tenant has only non-exclusive conditional access after 48 hours' notice. Possession and the 99-year term begin at commencement, not merely at execution.
Year-one base rent is $1,200,000 and is prepaid on commencement. The planned Phase One powered shell is at least 200,000 gross square feet and capable of receiving at least 200 MW.

oracle.terminal_when: The report preserves the execution-versus-commencement boundary and defers possession and rent recognition until the conditions are evidenced.

title: Classify phased capacity, funding, and service commencement
prompt: State which capacity and payments are presently committed. No financing materials, customer approval notice, final-plan approval, or ready-for-service notice is evidenced beyond the signed agreement.

observations.content: A signed colocation and master services agreement describes Phase One as 15 MW and Phase Two as an incremental 25 MW, for 40 MW only if Phase Two proceeds.

Phase One is a delivery obligation subject to its ready-for-service criteria. Phase Two requires acceptable financing materials and a written customer approval notice; disapproval or no notice leaves the parties with Phase One only.

Each phase's monthly colocation fee starts on that phase's commencement date after a ready-for-service notice. The Phase Two non-recurring charge is also conditioned on customer approval of final plans and specifications.
For direct supplier pass-through, approved invoices count toward the Phase Two NRC cap; over-cap costs stay with the operator unless approved in writing, and the same costs cannot be paid twice.

oracle.terminal_when: The report treats 15 MW as the only present delivery obligation, keeps Phase Two conditional, and preserves RFS and cost-control gates.

title: Separate a facilities study from construction and electric service
prompt: A 100 MW data-center applicant has signed only the study memorandum and the facilities study is incomplete. Classify current authority and quantify the tariff floors that would matter only after later agreements are executed.

observations.content: The applicant requested 100 MW and signed the memorandum used for a facilities study. The applicant reimburses the utility for that study. No construction service agreement or electric service contract is signed.
After the study, the utility and customer must enter a construction service agreement and a separate contract before facilities construction and service obligations apply.

The later contract must set minimum billing demand at no less than 85% of contract capacity, including ramp capacity. During the initial term, curtailing, reducing, suspending, or ending service does not avoid the monthly minimum charge unless the exit fee is paid.

The collateral requirement combines minimum charges for the ramp period, three years of minimum charges during the service term, and the exit fee. Connection and specified network-upgrade costs also require quantification in the later agreements.

oracle.terminal_when: The report limits current exposure to the reimbursable study and treats construction, service, minimum billing, and collateral as later contract gates.

title: Distinguish a definitive credit agreement from drawable cash
prompt: Can the project treat the disclosed facility as available construction cash at the cutoff? Reconcile the rounded aggregate and tranches, and state the next financing controls.

observations.content: The company entered a definitive non-recourse credit agreement described as up to approximately $43.8 million for its data-center business.

Rounded tranche disclosures are $18.5 million for a lease facility, $19.6 million for a term loan refinancing a 5 MW build-to-suit property, and $5.8 million for letters of credit or guaranty. The rounded components sum to $43.9 million.
The lender had not authorized use because conditions precedent remained unsatisfied. No amount had been drawn and no borrowing was available at the reporting date.
The disclosed financial covenants were not yet effective. Principal and interest on the three-year term loan would begin 30 days after drawdown, which had not occurred.

oracle.terminal_when: The report records a definitive agreement but zero availability and draw, while explaining the one-decimal rounding difference.

title: Preserve linked land, power, construction, and reversion terms
prompt: Assess whether the disclosed Denton project can be modeled as an effective lease assignment, independent land and power terms, and a fixed-price build. Identify the conditions and cash-flow sensitivities that must remain explicit.

observations.content: The Denton ground-lease assignment was executed but becomes effective only when the utility consents to the related power right-of-use agreement. The power right likewise depends on utility consent.

The roughly 64-acre ground lease runs through 2035 and terminates automatically if the power agreement ends. The 14-year power agreement has two seven-year extension options, but each extension requires the ground lease to be extended for the same period.

The campus was planned for an initial 262 MW and up to roughly 394 MW of power. Construction is cost of work plus a fee with a guaranteed maximum price that can be increased or reduced through change orders; certain costs may be reimbursed by the customer.
Monthly ground rent is $53,949.81 with periodic inflation adjustments. Improvements become the city landlord's property when the ground lease expires or terminates.

oracle.terminal_when: The report keeps consent, coterminous land-power terms, change-order exposure, reimbursement, and asset reversion in the underwriting model.
